context.abstract: Reflection positivity is tested on finite Gram matrices before it becomes an infinite-dimensional reconstruction problem. This paper proves a finite Schur--Feshbach criterion for Hermitian matrix families whose leading term is a rank-one reflected-vacuum block. If \[ q_\eps=\one\one^*+\eps H+\eps^2K+o(\eps^2), \] then the correct quotient-space expansion after eliminating the rank-one direction is \[ F_\eps =\eps PHP+ \eps^2P\bigl(K-n^{-1}Hee^*H\bigr)P+o(\eps^2), \qquad e=n^{-1/2}\one, \qquad P=I-ee^*. \] Thus the second-order test is not the naive compression \(PKP\), but the Schur--Feshbach corrected form \(P(K-n^{-1}Hee^*H)P\). The result gives necessary finite positivity conditions, strict sufficient margins, and a recursive null-sector test. The intended use is as a finite consistency check inside Wilson-loop/Osterwalder--Schrader constructions, where normalized reflected Wilson blocks may approach a rank-one collision limit. The claim is deliberately finite: the paper does not construct Yang--Mills theory and does not prove a mass gap. It identifies the finite coefficient data that any same-theory Wilson/OS realization must supply and respect before such blocks can be used in a reconstruction argument.
context.bounded_contribution: Finite Schur-Feshbach consistency test for normalized reflected Wilson Gram blocks near a rank-one collision limit.
explicit_non_claims: does not construct four-dimensional Yang-Mills theory
does not prove OS reconstruction for a continuum gauge field
does not prove a mass gap
context.title: A Finite Schur--Feshbach Consistency Test for Normalized Reflected Wilson Gram Blocks
